facts.statement: Azhdarcho lived about 92 million years ago in Uzbekistan during the middle Turonian stage of the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Azhdarcho is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of the Bissekty Formation (middle Turonian stage, about 92 million years ago) of Uzbekistan

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Azhdarcho is Azhdarcho lancicollis.
facts.quote: The type species is Azhdarcho lancicollis.

facts.statement: Most Azhdarcho individuals had a wingspan of 3 to 4 meters, though some remains suggest a span of 5 to 6 meters.
facts.quote: Most individuals were relatively small with an estimated wingspan of 3 - 4 m, but some remains indicate a larger wingspan of 5 - 6 m.

facts.statement: Lev A. Nesov discovered Azhdarcho fossils in the Kyzyl Kum desert between 1974 and 1981.
facts.quote: The fossil remains of Azhdarcho were recovered in the Kyzyl Kum desert (from the Taykarshinskaya unit of the Bissekty Formation) by Lev A. Nesov during expeditions to Central Asia in 1974–1981.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Azhdarcho is catalog number TsNIGRmuzey 1/11915 and consists of an anterior neck vertebra.
facts.quote: The type specimen, given the catalog number ЦНИГРмузей 1/11915 (TsNIGRmuzey), consists of an anterior neck vertebra.

facts.statement: Twelve paratypes of Azhdarcho include neck vertebrae, wing and leg elements, and jaw pieces.
facts.quote: Twelve paratypes were referred, including several other neck vertebrae, elements from the wing and leg, and pieces of the jaw.

facts.statement: Azhdarcho fossils were deposited at the F.N. Chernyshev Central Geologic Exploration Museum in St. Petersburg.
facts.quote: These specimens, along with other vertebrate fossils collected during the expeditions, were deposited at the F.N. Chernyshev Central Geologic Exploration Museum in St. Petersburg.

facts.statement: Nesov described the neck vertebrae of Azhdarcho lancicollis as extremely elongated and round in cross-section at mid-length.
facts.quote: In his description of the type specimen of Azhdarcho lancicollis, Nesov noted its distinctive neck vertebrae, which are extremely elongated and round in cross section at mid-length.

facts.statement: Subsequent research has not supported Nesov's suggestion of other species, leaving A. lancicollis as the only recognized species of Azhdarcho.
facts.quote: However, subsequent research has not followed this suggestion, and A. lancicollis is the only currently recognized species of Azhdarcho.

facts.statement: Nesov erected the subfamily Azhdarchinae within the family Pteranodontidae based on shared characteristics with Azhdarcho.
facts.quote: He pointed out similar characteristics in several other pterosaurs, and used them to erect the new subfamily Azhdarchinae, classified within the family Pteranodontidae.

facts.statement: Nesov initially placed Quetzalcoatlus and Arambourgiania in the subfamily Azhdarchinae, which was later reclassified as the family Azhdarchidae.
facts.quote: Nesov also referred Quetzalcoatlus and Arambourgiania (then known as Titanopteryx) to this subfamily, which was subsequently re-classified as the family Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: Azhdarcho is the type genus of the family Azhdarchidae and is placed within the clade Neoazhdarchia.
facts.quote: Below is a cladogram showing the phylogenetic placement of Azhdarcho within the clade Neoazhdarchia, more specifically within the family Azhdarchidae, of which Azhdarcho is the type genus.

facts.statement: The genus Azhdarcho was described by Nessov in 1984.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Nessov, 1984

facts.statement: Azhdarcho lived approximately 89 million years ago in Uzbekistan during the upper Turonian-Coniacian stages of the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Azhdarcho es un género de pterosaurios pterodactiloides que vivieron a partir de la última etapa del Cretácico, el Turoniense-Coniaciense superior, hace aproximadamente 89 millones de años, en lo que hoy es Uzbekistán.

facts.statement: Nesov noted that the articulation of Azhdarcho's vertebrae resulted in very limited neck flexibility.
facts.quote: In the original description of Azhdarcho, Nesov noted that because of the way the vertebrae articulated, the pterosaur would have had very limited flexibility in the neck.

facts.statement: Azhdarcho could not rotate its neck but could flex it vertically to some degree.
facts.quote: Azhdarcho could not rotate its neck at all, though it could flex the neck vertically to a certain degree.

facts.statement: Nesov suggested Azhdarcho may have fed like a modern skimmer, scooping prey from the water surface with its long neck.
facts.quote: Nesov suggested that pterosaurs like Azhdarcho may have fed in a manner similar to the modern skimmer, with their long necks allowing them to scoop prey from the water's surface and small depths without needing to dive.

facts.statement: Recent research suggests that large pterosaurs like Azhdarcho were probably not capable of skimming due to high energy and anatomical requirements.
facts.quote: However, recent research has shown that skimming requires more energy and anatomical specializations than previously thought, and that large pterosaurs like Azhdarcho probably were not capable of skimming.

facts.statement: Studies by Mark Witton suggest that azhdarchids like Azhdarcho were likely terrestrial stalkers similar to storks or ground hornbills.
facts.quote: However studies by Mark Witton points to a different direction suggesting that azhdarchids in general were terrestrial stalkers, akin to storks or ground hornbills.

facts.statement: The genus Azhdarcho lived from the Turonian to the Campanian stages, between 93.9 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Campanian (93.9 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The long neck of Azhdarcho may have allowed it to hunt in water or on the bottom while swimming, or to catch poorly flying vertebrates in the air.
rejected.quote: The long neck would also have allowed azhdarchids to hunt for food in the water or on the bottom while swimming, or to hunt poorly flying vertebrates in the air
